messages:
Nora: Quick UX check on the compact stackframe changes. Users want a denser default but still need clear affordances to expand frames and copy links. Figma: https://figma.com/file/redwood/compact-stackframes 
Samir: Runtime note: we stream frames with partial symbolication; expanding a frame triggers symbolication. Will add a 300ms debounce and show an inline skeleton. ETA ~2d.
Jules: Visual pattern: collapsed row shows function + file:line and a small chevron. On expand, slide out a details panel to the right (keeps context). Add a monospace preview plus a tiny `Copy frame link` button.
Anne: Accessibility: toggle needs aria-expanded and aria-controls. Ensure focus goes into the details panel and returns to the toggle on close. Add an offscreen label like `Expand stack frame details` for screen readers.
Priya: I'll test VoiceOver/NVDA on staging. Key checks: keyboard-only expand, live region announcing "Frame details loaded", and focus return. Also check color contrast for active frame highlight.
Nora: Microcopy: use sentence case for actions: `Copy frame link`, `Show source`. Toasts: `Frame link copied  View`. Keep text short.
Samir: Implementation question: what should the copy payload be? Propose short id `trace:abc123:frame:42` by default; full path opt-in in export. Short ids avoid exposing full request paths.
Jules: UX agree on short ids. In the details panel show both: short id prominent, full path collapsed under a disclosure "Show full path" for power users. 
deploy-bot: Rolled stackframe-compact to staging 2024-07-12T08:12:00Z.
Anne: Small keyboard nit: add shortcuts `E` to expand focused frame, `C` to copy frame link. Document in help. Ensure modifiers don't conflict with browser defaults.
Priya: I'll run a11y sweep after Samir's branch lands. If anything fails, I'll post specific a11y tickets.
Nora: Action items: (1) Jules update Figma with details panel + copy affordance, (2) Samir build branch with debounce, skeleton, aria attributes, (3) Anne verify focus management, (4) Priya run a11y checks. Thanks team.
